claims.summary: At (4,4), W = 2^(-l_1), on the events of lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split, cor:fine-mesh-function-tube at delta_0 = W and lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor at W, for N large: for nested lattice down-sets D_0 >= ... >= D_(K-1) (unions of W-cells) with extended 1-Lipschitz profiles phi_i in t = x - y, s = x + y, whose consecutive gaps phi_i - phi_(i+1) lie in [2 gamma W, 2 lambda gamma W] wherever strip i meets the square (gamma, lambda >= 1), every boundary of grid length at least l_0 > 0, and g = m W y* sum 1_(D_i) of discrete cost at most 2, with v = m y*: |D(g)| <= C sqrt(N log N)(1 + (1 + 1/l_0)(1 + lambda (log(v/2))^(-1/4))) + C l_0^(-1) sqrt N (log(4 lambda gamma))^(3/4) (log(v/2))^(-1/4), C universal; at the target when lambda <= (log(v/2))^(1/4) and either gamma <= v or log(4 lambda gamma) <= (log N)^(2/3) (log(v/2))^(1/3). The case lambda = gamma = 1 is cor:translate-staircase-stacks; lambda = 1, gamma = p gives translates p cells apart, at the target for p <= v.
claims.assessment: Working proof, passed with corrections by one medium reviewer: the interpolating ramp R between consecutive extended profiles has |g - R| <= a/K and Lipschitz constant C (a/K)/(gamma W); lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split at the mesh of the stack's least width 2 gamma K W bounds R, with Lambda at most C(lambda + 2)a by a cell count along the stack (the uniform mesh's loss); the same lemma at the mesh W bounds R minus its cell averages, Lambda at most C a counted strip by strip; cor:fine-mesh-function-tube at the coarse mesh near 2 lambda gamma W bounds the texture, the cell average of g - R; lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (c) bounds a and the case v >= sqrt(N/log N).
claims.rationale: Extends cor:translate-staircase-stacks from translates to distinct nested staircases with comparable gaps, a larger subclass of the one-height chains cor:coarse-discrete-sufficiency (b) asks; the gap ratio enters linearly through step (1)'s uniform mesh, a property of the method.
claims.next_action: The adapted partition through lem:local-factor-discrepancy (b) on stacks with runs of narrow gaps among wide ones, for a bound in (log lambda)^(3/4), then a stopping-time combination with regrouping for general gap patterns.
